purpose: Internal feasibility test of proposed safety decision reasoning, not a historic Oxford safety case, a patient incident or an expert reference.
temporalDesign: The original OUH evaluation was published before the fictional 18 November 2026 proposed deployment decision, so its public findings are permissible external background, but not evidence of local product/control effectiveness.

sourceGroundedFacts.locator: PDF index 4 / printed p.5, executive summary
sourceGroundedFacts.summary: 37.3% of 398 logged AVT uses reportedly required accuracy edits; reasons noted as 126 clinical accuracy, 43 spelling/grammar, 24 invented information.
sourceGroundedFacts.caveat: Categories should not be summed as independent cases; figures are reported usage/editing entries, not patient harm.

sourceGroundedFacts.summary: More challenging inaccuracies were described in complex, qualitative and multi-voice encounters, compared with structured consultations.
sourceGroundedFacts.caveat: Heterogeneous observational associations; not a validated model-specific risk multiplier.

sourceGroundedFacts.summary: The report describes no randomisation or controls, considerable self-report and no direct patient outcome/systematic error tracking.
sourceGroundedFacts.caveat: Not valid to infer true error incidence or clinician-review sensitivity.

sourceGroundedFacts.summary: OUH recommends phased use-case deployment and timely review of outputs after encounters.
sourceGroundedFacts.caveat: A recommendation to review does not establish that any separate organisation has implemented or verified the control.

syntheticScenarioFacts: Fictional appointments are 15 minutes long; some involve multiple problems or a relative speaking.
Fictional service proposes standalone AVT browser workflow with manual copy to EPR.
An SOP says each treating clinician must review the note before sign-off, but no genuine signed operational implementation evidence is supplied.
Fictional six-user feasibility walkthrough shows users can operate the interface but contains no rigorous seeded-error detection assessment.
Supplier accuracy and OUH publication are cited as support for review effectiveness, although neither demonstrates the local control's clinical effectiveness.
No local audit of corrected AVT drafts versus signed EPR notes or controlled test of multi-speaker attribution is supplied.
No recorded accountable owner is provided for the AVT-to-EPR transfer safeguard.
The team proposes a Low category for one hazard without providing an actual risk-method document or evidence of accepted risk.

context.intendedPurpose: Draft outpatient consultation notes for treating clinician review before entry into the EPR; no diagnosis, triage, prescribing or autonomous actions.
context.careSetting: Fictional adult general-medicine follow-up outpatient clinics, England
context.workflowDescription: Fictional 15-minute outpatient appointments; some multi-problem consultations involve a relative. AVT creates a draft in a stand-alone browser interface. The treating clinician reviews and edits it, copies the final text into the EPR and signs it. No automated EPR integration.
context.relevantPopulation: Adult outpatient attendees, including encounters with more than one speaker
scopeLimits: Synthetic prospective scenario as at 18 November 2026, NOT an Oxford deployment decision
No real supplier, trust, patient or internal local safety case
Not for clinical recommendations or automated action

assessmentInput.proposedDecision: Fictional project team proposes proceeding with deployment across these clinics on the basis that mandated clinician sign-off and a local SOP sufficiently mitigate inaccurate notes, and assigns a provisional 'Low' residual-risk category.

hazards.description: An AVT-generated note may omit, misattribute or invent clinically relevant encounter details.
hazards.potentialHarm: An undetected inaccurate signed record could influence subsequent management or safety-netting.

hazards.description: A note edited in the stand-alone AVT interface may differ from the content finally copied into and signed in the EPR.
hazards.potentialHarm: An incorrect or outdated final record could affect downstream care.

controls.statement: Treating clinician reviews and signs each generated note, including comparison of clinically significant details before copying to EPR.
localDependencies: Time and opportunity to check the note
Corrected note matching the EPR version
controls.reviewerNotes: Fictional team relies on an SOP, a basic workflow walkthrough, an external NHS evaluation and an unspecified supplier claim; no local sensitivity-to-clinically-consequential-error testing is provided.

controls.statement: Manual copying of the edited note into the EPR followed by clinician sign-off.
localDependencies: AVT and EPR draft versions remain aligned
Final text is the reviewed text

evidence.title: TheHill and Oxford University Hospitals: Ambient Voice Technology in Acute Services - An Evaluation
evidence.applicabilityNote: Published experience across four AVT products and heterogeneous OUH workflows; not this fictional trust, product/model version, or local verification process.
limitations: Service evaluation; no randomisation or control group
Self-reported, heterogeneous and not designed for systematic patient-outcome or error tracking
Editing frequency is not patient-harm frequency or local clinician-review sensitivity
Reported reason categories may overlap; source calls 24/398 6.2% although this ratio does not exactly equal 6.2%

evidence.title: Fictional proposed note-review SOP (not a reviewed real document)
evidence.applicabilityNote: Case stipulates that the project team says an SOP exists; no signed or operationally verified local evidence is supplied.
limitations: Fabricated for methodological challenge; not a genuine trust policy

evidence.title: Fictional supplier accuracy assertion
evidence.applicabilityNote: Fictional general accuracy claim without demonstrated applicability to this model, population or workflow.
limitations: Synthetic placeholder, not a real manufacturer claim or evaluation

evidence.title: Fictional six-user feasibility walkthrough description
evidence.applicabilityNote: Fictional usability walkthrough demonstrates that draft review/sign-off can be completed, but not clinically consequential error-detection sensitivity.
limitations: No raw observations, adjudicated reference errors or independent reviewer evidence

residualRiskClaims.claimedReasoning: The project team asserts that mandatory clinician review makes residual documentation inaccuracy risk Low. This is a synthetic claim, not a clinical risk assessment.
No separately supported residual-risk category is presented for the manual AVT-to-EPR handoff.

independentReviewerQuestions: Is the stated intended use and scenario boundary sufficiently defined for a DCB0160 local decision challenge?
What patient-harm mechanisms, including interacting workflow dependencies, should be considered or justifiably excluded?
For each claimed safeguard, what is actually evidenced: existence, implementation, verification or clinical effectiveness?
Can an external OUH service evaluation or fictional supplier assertion support the local effectiveness claim? Why or why not?
What does the proposed residual-risk reasoning establish under an organisation-approved, versioned method? What remains indeterminate?
What review, escalation, additional local evidence or governance decision would be required? Identify accountable parties without inventing authorisation.
Which concerns are clinically material, unsubstantiated, or potentially false alarms? Record competing explanations and disagreements.
notes: This is NOT the original Oxford trust, supplier, model, staff or clinical safety decision.
The reported Oxford findings are external background; all local assumptions, intended workflow and risk claims are fabricated and clearly labelled.
Do not publish or score expert findings before blind independent CSO adjudication.
